summary: Lake County, OR lookout site: a 1930 Forest Service lookout, a 1935 L-5 cab and a 1950s tower reported gone; a 2020 blog describes a closed, decaying lookout nearby.

facts.design: L-5 cab (1935), replaced in the 1950s by a 10-foot treated timber R-6 tower
facts.status_note: The register and firelookout.com say the tower is gone; a 2020 blog describes an abandoned, closed and decaying lookout about a third of a mile up an old road from the Palisade Rocks trailhead. The sources do not say whether it is the same structure

staffing.status: Forest Service lookout opened in 1930; Camp Bly CCC enrollees stationed there in 1937

access.note: A 2020 blog says the abandoned lookout is closed to visitors for safety reasons and is not maintained; the blog places the Palisade Rocks trail in the Gearhart Mountain Wilderness

visit.trail_note: Trailhead at the end of National Forest road 012, rough but passable in July 2020, with no facilities. The blog says the old lookout is closed to visitors

events.note: A Klamath Forest Protective Association lookout on the summit reported the Lakeview fire (1926 newspaper quoted on the Forest Lookouts page); unclear whether it stood on the later lookout's spot
Forest Service lookout opened July 1, 1930 with Lester Collins in charge (Lake County Tribune, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page)
L-5 cab built about two miles southeast of the summit
Two Camp Bly CCC enrollees stationed at the lookout as an emergency station, occupied only in extremely hot weather
Cab replaced by a 10-foot treated timber R-6 tower in the 1950s (exact year not given)
Registered June 4, 2011 as US 1026, OR 384; nominated by Ray Kresek
Blog describes an abandoned lookout near Palisade Rocks as closed to visitors, not maintained and decaying

corrections.why: Both FFLOS and firelookout.com describe a 10-foot treated timber R-6 tower, and 10 feet is about 3.0 m. The brief's 3.7 m (about 12 feet) matches neither source. Assumes the 10-foot figure is the tower height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1930 Forest Service lookout (Lake County Tribune, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) and the 1935 L-5 cab (FFLOS, firelookout.com) may not be the same structure; the sources do not say. The story gives both dates.

FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower is gone. The 2020 blog describes an abandoned, closed and decaying lookout near the Palisade Rocks trailhead. The sources do not say whether it is the same structure, so status stays gone with a note.

notes_for_editor: Status conflict: FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower is gone, but a July 2020 blog describes an abandoned, closed, decaying lookout about a third of a mile up an old road from the Palisade Rocks trailhead (NF-012). Whether it is the same structure is unknown from these sources; worth checking before changing status. Brief access 'unknown' is set to closed on the blog's word only. Brief height 3.7 m does not match the 10-foot tower. The 1926 summit lookout may or may not be the 1930 lookout.
